Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF UNKNOWN MATERIALS HAVE BEEN RELEASED INTO A DITCH AN CULVERT THAT LEAD TO LITTLE CYPRESS BAYOU THAT THEN LEADS TO SABINE RIVER. properties.content:
Report Details

Nearest City: Medford, OK
Location: NATURAL GAS FACILITY
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: NATURAL GAS
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 36.805679, -97.734770 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report Description
AS RECEIVED VIA DHS NOC: OVERVIEW: AT 1531 EST, OPEN SOURCE MEDIA REPORTED THE TOWN OF MEDFORD, OK (POP. 996) IS ISSUING A NON-MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER DUE TO A LEAK THAT DEVELOPED AT A NATURAL GAS FACILITY ON 29 FEB. DUE TO AN INCREASE IN WINDS, THE TOWN HAS DECIDED TO ISSUE THE ADVISORY AT 1600 EST TODAY. FEMA REGION VI REPORTS LOCAL OFFICIALS WILL ISSUE A NON-MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER FOR THE TOWN OF MEDFORD DUE TO DANGEROUS LEVELS OF NATURAL GAS IN THE AREA. A MEETING OF THE TOWN EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY WILL OCCUR AT 1800 EST TO DETERMINE IF A MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER WILL BE RELEASED. MEDFORD, OK IS 93 MILES NORTH OF OKLAHOMA CITY, OK. STATE AND LOCAL FIRST RESPONDERS ARE ON-SCENE, AND A PORTION OF US HIGHWAY 81 HAS BEEN SHUT DOWN. A LOCAL JAIL IS BEING EVACUATED IN THE INCIDENT AREA AND INMATES WILL BE TRANSPORTED TO KAY COUNTY JAIL. THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT STATES A LONG TERM CARE FACILITY HAS BEEN CONTACTED BY THE LOCAL FIRE CHIEF REGARDING THE EVACUATION OF THEIR RESIDENTS. THE LAST PLACE OF TRACKING WAS AT THE RP ADDRESS.

properties.content:

Location: 600 LEHL STREET
Incident Type: FIXED

Suspected Responsible Party: IOWA GOLD DISTRIBUTING
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.970703, -91.659149 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 70000 gallon
Report Description
AT APPROXIMATELY 0800CST ON 24NOV2016, FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS DISPATCHED TO A FIRE/EXPLOSION AT A WASTE OIL RECYCLING FACILITY. AS A RESULT OF IMPACT TWO 25,000 GALLON AND ONE 20,000 GALLON STORAGE TANK WERE COMPROMISED. AN ESTIMATED (UNCONFIRMED) 30,000-70,000 GALLONS OF WASTE OIL DISCHARGED. THE REPORTING SOURCE SUSPECTS THAT MAJORITY OF THE OIL BURNED OFF IN THE FIRE, YET AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT IMPACTED TWO NEARBY DITCHES (EVENTUALLY RUNS INTO AN UNNAMED TRIBUTARY OF THE WAPSIPINICON RIVER). STATE REPORTED THAT THE DITCHES ARE STAINED, HOWEVER, THERE IS NO VISIBLE SHEEN OR KNOWN WATER IMPACT. INITIAL CAUSE OF INCIDENT IS UNKNOWN, POSSIBLY DUE TO A FAULTY FURNACE. NO INJURIES OR EVACUATIONS WERE REPORTED, HOWEVER, CITIZENS WERE ADVISED TO SHELTER IN PLACE. TWO NEIGHBORING BUILDINGS WERE ALSO DAMAGED
